text:
Evan (Sales): Heads up — Cascade (financial analytics startup) kicked off a POC. They want to bring a custom 34B llama variant AND use our KV cache for session-based retrievals. Also flagged: KMS for customer-managed keys and a short security questionnaire. Can we do a quick compatibility sweep?

Tess (SE): Thanks. Do we have the model artifact details (hf url / config)? KV cache usually ok but depends on sequence length and mmap layout.

Evan (Sales): They shared this link and note: https://files.cascade.ai/models/llama-34b-v1.tar.gz They said quantized int8, custom tokenizer.

Priya (Solutions): Quick checklist: (1) tokenizer compat, (2) kv-cache layout (32-bit vs 64-bit offsets), (3) supported quant format (q4/q8), (4) KMS + audit logs. I can own the tokenizer and eval checks.

Marco (Infra): For KV cache: our runtime expects per-layer KV packed little-endian float16 by default for that model family; int8 quant will need an adapter. If they use an mmap-backed kv shard, we can mount it on Dedicated. Need to confirm memory map flags and alignment.

Lena (Security): Send the security questionnaire PDF. High-level: CMEK via AWS KMS/HSM ok, we need SC-2 attestation for backup retention. Also ask them about PHI/PII — if they plan to send sensitive financial transaction data, Private deployment may be required.

Evan (Sales): They said no PHI, but transaction-level user IDs might be sent. They prefer Hosted for speed but open to Dedicated for encryption. Pricing question: will this push them to a reserved capacity?

Tess (SE): If KV cold-starts are high (long context windows with few cache hits), cost per token will spike; we can recommend prefix caching and prewarm policies. For Dedicated: baseline commit calc = expected rps * seq_len * concurrency. I can draft numbers.

Priya (Solutions): Also note: tokenizer mismatch often breaks embeddings. Ask them to provide a sample encoded id sequence and a small prompt for validation. We'll run a quick determinism test.

Evan (Sales): Action items: Tess — run compatibility pass on model artifact + quant checks. Marco — confirm KV mmap/adapter path and whether Dedicated needed for performance. Lena — scan the questionnaire and list hard blockers. Priya — prepare the eval harness + pricing sketch.

Tess (SE): Got it. Quick thing — can someone paste the runtime adapter snippet for int8 conversion? I have a test harness but it's missing the wrapper.

Marco (Infra): Paste below — this is the minimal shim we use to translate q8 files into runtime-format on Dedicated nodes: ```bash
# convert-quant.sh
python -c "from rw_runtime.tools import q_adapter; q_adapter.convert('input.q8', '/tmp/adapter_out', format='packed_kv')"
# then mount /tmp/adapter_out as kv_dir in runtime config
```

Lena (Security): Qs from the questionnaire: 1) Do you require customer-managed keys (yes/no)? 2) Do you store logs with user content? 3) Retention period for backups? Please get answers in writing.

Evan (Sales): I'll get them to confirm. One more: they asked about SLAs for canary failover to a smaller (non-quantized) variant if latency regressions happen after rollout. Is that supported?

Tess (SE): We can do automatic fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., float16 34B) if health checks fail, but perf/cost differ. Need to make sure model is in catalog or we mirror artifacts. That also affects pricing because fallback may consume more GPU.

Priya (Solutions): Pricing note to include: stealth POC discount (30% off hosted), Dedicated sizing estimate with commit numbers, and a safety buffer for fallback (recommend +20% capacity). I'll draft a short spreadsheet.

ops-bot: deployment-check — Dedicated pool availability in us-west-2: 3x A100 pools currently free for new reservations.

Marco (Infra): Re KV: if they insist on mmap and shared filesystem, we need to validate NFS locking semantics. Prefer local SSD + prewarm sync.

Evan (Sales): Great. I'll coordinate with the customer for the tokenizer sample and the security answers. Back in ~24 hours with updates. :thumbsup:

Tess (SE): I'll start the artifact compatibility run now, will post results here.

Priya (Solutions): I'll prep the eval harness and pricing spreadsheet, pinging legal for template language on CMEK.

Lena (Security): I'll highlight anything that forces Private deployment.

Evan (Sales): Thanks team. If anything blocks the POC start, call me out.
